messages:
marta: FYI rack-12 TOR1 showing packet drops intermittently for the last 20m. Dedicated-pool-43 tail latency + token-timeouts spiking. :frowning:

samir: ugh, saw alerts. Is it NIC-level or TOR? any pcap? :eyes:

marta: initial tcpdump shows retransmits on port 9150 and drops correlated with a particular host (10.11.12.77). snippet:
```
15:22:11.123456 IP 10.11.12.77.9150 > 10.11.12.1.443: Flags [P.], seq 1234:1300, ack 987, win 256
15:22:11.130000 IP 10.11.12.77 > 10.11.12.1: RTO retransmission
```

marta: not seeing CPU/GPU overload on that host, it's mostly egress bursts. could be a flaky SFP or noisy tenant causing port hogging.

kai: can we try a port-shuffle on TOR1 to move that host to another leaf port and see if drops follow? minimal disruption if we do quick L2 move.

olivia: port-shuffle ok from infra side, but pool-43 has AZ pinning. we cannot move tenants off-rack if they require local NVLink or low-latency. need to check which allocations on 10.11.12.77.

julian: running quick query: `SELECT tenant, allocation FROM allocs WHERE host='10.11.12.77'` -> returns tenant_a (dedicated), tenant_b (shared burst), infra-agent (monitoring). tenant_a pinned to rack-12 for latency SLAs.

samir: if tenant_a is pinned, port shuffle may still help if issue is TOR port or NIC. alternative: preemptive quarantine of the offending host and move tenant_b and infra-agent off the port, keep tenant_a but remap its traffic via TOR fallback path? cost and latency implications though.

marta: proposal: quarantine host 10.11.12.77 (egress block for non-pinned tenants), trigger warm-backfill for tenant_b to a sibling rack in same AZ, and run verification for 10m. ops-bot + traceroute checks before and after.

ops-bot: Migration job 8823 queued: warm-backfill tenant_b -> rack-14 (same AZ). Estimated runtime 2m. Will emit events.

olivia: agree, tenant_a remains, tenant_b gets moved. watch out for burst credits; moving tenants within AZ keeps egress costs low. also add temporary rate-limit on 10.11.12.77:9150 for 30m.

julian: applied egress policer (tc) on host: `tc qdisc add dev eth0 root tbf rate 200mbit burst 15kb latency 50ms` - monitoring.

marta: after quarantine and policer, retransmits dropped to near zero in the last 3m. ops-bot shows migration job 8823 success. tail latencies for pool-43 back to baseline. :thumbsup:

samir: nice. follow-ups: replace SFP on TOR1 tomorrow, schedule host NIC diagnostics, and add a small detector to flag single-host egress spikes that exceed 70% of port capacity for >1m. costs: minimal since we kept actions intra-AZ, but note warm-backfill uses reserved warm pool (metered) so bill owner will see small transient.

marta: noted. creating short runbook and follow-up ticket for HW swap and detector. thanks all.

julian: ping @networking-team for SFP replacement windows.

kai: great triage, closing thread once runbook is posted.
